title: Cache and persistence
summary: Cache only reused results whose recomputation cost justifies memory and storage pressure.

blocks.text: Cache only reused results whose recomputation cost justifies memory and storage pressure.

items: Caching is lazy; it materializes only when an action executes.
Persisting a huge one-use DataFrame usually hurts more than it helps.
Unpersist data when it is no longer useful.
Check storage usage and recomputation before assuming cache is beneficial.

blocks.code:
# Run in an existing SparkSession named spark; bounded toy data.
base = spark.createDataFrame(
    [("NO", True), ("NO", False), ("CH", True)],
    ["country", "is_active"],
).filter("country IS NOT NULL").persist()
try:
    base.count()  # materialize intentionally for this demonstration
    by_country = base.groupBy("country").count()
    active_rows = base.filter("is_active")
    by_country.show()   # action while the cached base is retained
    active_rows.show()  # another action before release
finally:
    base.unpersist()
# Do not cache every DataFrame in production; measure actual reuse and cost.
blocks.title: Example
blocks.explanation: Both lazy results are consumed by actions while the cached base is retained; unpersist runs in finally. Not executed during preparation: run it once on your target Spark runtime before relying on it.
